hazard-classes-addressed.cleared-because: Topology first, so the named revisions are the ones the brief means: 'merge-base f99b8d7 fcc026b = 810a88e30cb880591d99e869c9626489323e1ae6', '810a88e full = 810a88e30cb880591d99e869c9626489323e1ae6', 'parents of 1b8de3e = 1b8de3e01e3d75923996766a8f5643a9b86c4260 f99b8d723d460aeb29eeea33ad0fbb6046debc02 fcc026ba78203eb4a3cb45cb0bdf9dc2373b79b8'. So 1b8de3e is exactly the two-parent merge of the M6-P7 head into which the M6-P5 head was brought, and 810a88e is their merge base. The two diffs are byte-identical in size: 'A bytes 13876 lines 258' and 'B bytes 13876 lines 258'. They touch the same four paths and no others, in the same order: 'diff --git a/.github/workflows/gates.yml b/.github/workflows/gates.yml', 'diff --git a/test/behaviors.json b/test/behaviors.json', 'diff --git a/test/gate-registry.test.ts b/test/gate-registry.test.ts', 'diff --git a/witness/mechanism-index-claim-file-rule.json b/witness/mechanism-index-claim-file-rule.json'. That is M6-P5's reviewed change and nothing beside it: a workflow step, one test, one appended registry row, one removed witness spec. Ignoring index lines alone the texts still differ ('IDENTICAL_MINUS_INDEX_LINES: false'), at exactly one place, a hunk header: 'FIRST_DIVERGENCE line 61  A: "@@ -1159,5 +1159,6 @@"  B: "@@ -1153,5 +1153,6 @@"'. The full hunk-header lists differ in that one element and agree on the other four: A ['@@ -74,9 +74,17 @@ jobs:','@@ -85,15 +93,24 @@ jobs:','@@ -1159,5 +1159,6 @@','@@ -1659,6 +1659,151 @@ test("the gates workflow checks out the pull-request head branch by name (ref: g','@@ -1,24 +0,0 @@'] against B ['@@ -74,9 +74,17 @@ jobs:','@@ -85,15 +93,24 @@ jobs:','@@ -1153,5 +1153,6 @@','@@ -1659,6 +1659,151 @@ test("the gates workflow checks out the pull-request head branch by name (ref: g','@@ -1,24 +0,0 @@']. I did NOT accept that on its face, because the brief allows index-line differences only. I derived it instead. The differing header is in test/behaviors.json, the append-only registry, and it is an offset only, not content: normalizing hunk headers as well as index lines makes the two texts equal, 'IDENTICAL_MINUS_INDEX_AND_HUNK_OFFSETS: true'. The offset is 1159 minus 1153 = 6, and 'line counts: 810a88e 1158 f99b8d7 1164 delta 6', those 6 lines being M6-P7's own six registry rows added between the merge base and f99b8d7 (git diff 810a88e f99b8d7 -- test/behaviors.json shows '@@ -1097,6 +1097,12 @@' adding m6-p7-codex-argv-maps-grant, m6-p7-codex-observer-reads-real-capture, m6-p7-families-from-two-vocabularies, m6-p7-harness-environment-declared, m6-p7-review-executor-from-charter and m6-p7-harness-environment-credential-store-pointer). The two index lines that differ are the same file's pre- and post-image ('index 7724cb6..4814eed 100644' against 'index e9ca8ec..0d15ff0 100644'), for the same reason; the other three index lines are identical on both sides. So the one non-index difference is the arithmetic consequence of applying the identical patch to a pre-image six lines longer, which is what an append-only registry resolved as a union is supposed to produce, and it is not a difference in what the merge brought. Both sides add the identical single row, quoted from each diff: '+  "m6-p5-phase-from-pr-title": "the pull-request gates step takes --phase from a phase branch, else from the title's leading Mn-Pn: lowercased, else the branch name, and the title's shell syntax runs nothing"'. Registry health at this head: 'PARSES OK, rows: 1162', with 'PRESENT  m6-p5-phase-from-pr-title' and 'PRESENT' for all six M6-P7 rows (m6-p7-codex-argv-maps-grant, m6-p7-codex-observer-reads-real-capture, m6-p7-families-from-two-vocabularies, m6-p7-harness-environment-declared, m6-p7-review-executor-from-charter, m6-p7-harness-environment-credential-store-pointer), resolved by name and never by count. No finding. Scope of this check, and what it does not cover: the comparison excludes delivery/ by the brief's own pathspec, so paperwork brought by the merge is outside it; and it compares the merge against M6-P5's diff, so it says nothing about M6-P5's change itself, which was reviewed under M6-P5.

hazard-classes-addressed.probed: Ran the test named by the fix for CR-M6P7A-01 (test/codex-review.test.ts:305, the 'credential-store pointer' test) green at this head, then applied witness members from witness/m6-p7-harness-environment-credential-store-pointer.json by hand after copying src/review.ts aside, rebuilt, and observed the test red on each. The brief asked for one member; I applied two of the spec's three, because the first reddens on a downstream unrelated assertion and only the second reddens on the dangerous state itself.
hazard-classes-addressed.cleared-because:
Green first, with dist/ built from this head by npm run build: 'PASS an executor declaring a credential-store pointer never gives the reviewer the kernel's HOME or its credentials: the dispatch is refused before anything is created, and the harness join sets every pointer back to its harness-owned target (1204.483481ms)', 'i tests 1', 'i pass 1', 'i fail 0', 'i skipped 0'. Member 1 of the spec (src/review.ts, 'if (refusedPointer !== undefined) {' to 'if (false) {', applied at src/review.ts:547, rebuilt): 'FAIL an executor declaring a credential-store pointer never gives the reviewer the kernel's HOME or its credentials: ... (436.884982ms)' with 'AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: The input did not match the regular expression /declares an environment the kernel refuses: the allowlist extension entry HOME is a credential-store pointer/. Input: "tiphys review: no served model was observed: codex exec --json names no served model on any event it writes (thread, turn and item rows carry none), and neither the reviewer's own text nor the requested model is an observation"', at test/codex-review.test.ts:337. That is red, and it is red for the right reason: with the refusal arm disabled the dispatch is no longer refused before anything is created, so it proceeds and dies later elsewhere. But its assertion message is about a missing refusal, not about the leak, so on its own it is a weaker witness than the hazard deserves. So I applied member 2 as well (delete the harness-join line '      env[name] = target;' from src/review.ts; a node check confirmed 'occurrences of member-2 find string: 1', so the edit is the spec's and is unambiguous; rebuilt). It reddens directly on the dangerous state: 'FAIL an executor declaring a credential-store pointer ... (1171.378142ms)', 'AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: the reviewer was handed HOME /tmp/tiphys-codex-review-ldbx4B/kernel-home and GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL /tmp/tiphys-codex-review-ldbx4B/kernel-gitconfig', actual '{ reviewerHomeIsKernelHome: true, reviewerHomeGitCredentials: 'https://x:SECRET-TOKEN@github.com
', reviewerGitConfigGlobal: '[credential]
	helper = store
' }' against expected '{ reviewerHomeIsKernelHome: false, reviewerHomeGitCredentials: null, reviewerGitConfigGlobal: '' }', at test/codex-review.test.ts:388. So the guard is not merely present, it fails when the reviewer actually receives the kernel's HOME and the credential stored in it, which is exactly CR-M6P7A-01's hazard; and two structurally different members redden it, so it guards the class and not one mutation. src/review.ts was copied to src/review.ts.witnessbak before the first mutation and restored from that copy after each, never with git checkout -- <path>. After restoring and deleting the backup, 'git status --short' prints exactly one line, '?? delivery/review/m6-p7-hazard-d.json', this verdict file, so no tracked file is modified and no stray file is left; src/review.ts shows an empty git diff --stat. dist/ was rebuilt from the restored source afterwards. Transliteration declared, per the repository's ASCII rule: in the captured reporter output quoted above I replaced U+2714 HEAVY CHECK MARK with 'PASS', 1 occurrence; U+2716 HEAVY MULTIPLICATION X with 'FAIL', 3 occurrences; U+2139 INFORMATION SOURCE with 'i', 4 occurrences. Nothing else in the quoted output was changed, and the ellipses shown are my elisions of the test's own repeated title. No finding. What this check does not cover: it re-proves the named fix at this head, and by the owner's rule it does not redo review A or check C, so the rest of M6-P7's behavior rests on those.
